data.name: Auction Verification
data.abstract: We modeled a simultaneous multi-round auction with BPMN models, transformed the latter to Petri nets, and used a model checker to verify whether certain outcomes of the auction are possible or not.

intro_paper.title: Analyzing and Predicting Verification of Data-Aware Process Models – a Case Study with Spectrum Auctions
intro_paper.authors: Elaheh Ordoni, Jakob Bach, Ann-Katrin Fleck

variables.name: process.b1.capacity
variables.description: Capacity (max number of products to win) of Bidder 1.

variables.name: process.b2.capacity
variables.description: Capacity (max number of products to win) of Bidder 2.

variables.name: process.b3.capacity
variables.description: Capacity (max number of products to win) of Bidder 3.

variables.name: process.b4.capacity
variables.description: Capacity (max number of products to win) of Bidder 4.

variables.name: property.winner
variables.description: Bidder currently verified as winner of the product (0 if only price verified).

variables.name: verification.result
variables.description: Binary verification result - is the verified outcome possible?

additional_info.summary: Our code to prepare the dataset and to make predictions is available here: https://github.com/Jakob-Bach/Analyzing-Auction-Verification
additional_info.purpose: The dataset was created as part of a scientific study. The goal was to find out whether one could replace costly verification of complex process models (here: simultaneous multi-round auctions, as used for auctioning frequency spectra) with predictions of the outcome.
additional_info.instances_represent: Each instance represents one verification run. Verification checks whether a particular price is possible for a particular product, and (for only some of the instances) whether a particular bidder might win the product to that price.
additional_info.citation: If you use this dataset in experiments for a scientific publication, we would be happy if you could cite our paper: https://www.doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2022.3154445
